title: A General-Purpose Predictive World Model
content: World models are considered advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems capable of simulating and understanding the various dynamics of the real world. In fact, these models represent significant progress in AI, as they have established a new paradigm for learning compact, predictive representations that enable AI agents to reason, simulate, and act in complex environments. Despite this not being a new concept within the AI community, the main challenges lie in the existing implementation, which spans variational generative models, contrastive predictive methods, and imagination-based latent reinforcement learning, all of which remain completely fragmented in both design and theoretical understanding. It is on this basis that this paper proposes a generalised framework architecture that unifies representation learning, latent dynamics modelling, and policy optimisation within a single probabilistic design. The new architectural design proposes integrating generative objectives, including reconstruction and variational inference, with a predictive objective, namely contrastive and self-supervised learning. The whole idea in this case is to fully leverage structured latent states and imagination-based rollouts for efficient decision-making. Moreover, the motivation is that, by abstracting and synthesising key principles from related concepts and architectures, the proposed unified model formulation can provide a coherent foundation for analysing, designing, and extending world-model-based systems. Therefore, this study argues that the current unified perspective advances the development of scalable, data-efficient, and general-purpose agents capable of learning, predicting, and planning in high-dimensional, partially observable environments.
